title: Runtime Content Boundaries
interviewAnswer: The tracked Angular shell loads a selected runtime content source through stable HTTP contracts, so proprietary curriculum does not need to live in the public source repository.
explanation: The public demo, private authoring source, generated runtime staging, and future authenticated content origin have separate responsibilities.
summary: This synthetic lesson demonstrates the same loading and navigation contracts as the full platform without publishing interview preparation material.

sections.heading: Separate the shell from the material
body: Angular owns routing, interaction, accessibility, responsive layout, and rendering. A selected content source supplies catalogs, course manifests, modules, and lesson payloads at runtime.
That separation lets the public repository demonstrate engineering quality while the authored curriculum remains in an authorized private system.

callout.title: Public by construction
callout.text: A clean public clone starts with deliberately synthetic demo data. It does not fall back to or reconstruct private curriculum.

sections.heading: Keep one runtime contract
body: The application reads the same URL shape regardless of whether data came from the tracked demo, an authorized local directory, or a future authenticated origin.
Page components stay independent of storage details, which keeps a later S3 or API delivery change out of the presentation layer.

sections.heading: Fail closed before publication
body: Public-readiness checks reject private directories, generated runtime assets, local absolute paths, credential-shaped files, and imports from private authoring code.
CI validates both the demo dataset and a minimal schema fixture before running unit tests and the production build.

callout.title: Why two datasets?
callout.text: The demo supports human review; the smaller fixture isolates schema and loader contracts for deterministic CI diagnostics.

keyTakeaways: The public repository contains product code and synthetic demo data, not proprietary curriculum.
All content modes satisfy one runtime HTTP contract.
Automated checks make the privacy boundary testable rather than aspirational.
versionNotes: Synthetic public demonstration content; not part of the learning curriculum.

followUps.question: Where will production content come from?
followUps.answer: The intended delivery boundary is an authenticated content origin. Storage and authorization can evolve without changing page components.
